column2: On the authority of Abū al-ʿAbbās Sahl ibn Saʿd al-Sāʿidī (may Allah the Exalted be pleased with him), who said: A man came to the Prophet (Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace) and said:

“O Messenger of Allah, direct me to a deed which, if I do it, Allah will love me and people will love me.” He said: “Renounce the world and Allah will love you, and renounce what people possess and people will love you.”
A ḥasan hadith, reported by Ibn Mājah and others with ḥasan chains.
“Renounce the world”: limit yourself to what is necessary of it.
“Allah will love you”: because you have turned away from what He commanded you to turn away from.
“And renounce what people possess”: of worldly things.

“People will love you”: because their hearts are naturally disposed to love the world, and whoever contends with a person over what he loves, he dislikes and detests him, while whoever does not oppose him in it, he loves.
Renouncing the world is among the causes of Allah the Exalted's love for His servant and of people's love for him.

There is nothing wrong with striving for what earns people's love, provided it is not unlawful; rather, it is recommended, as shown by the command to spread the greeting of peace and the other things that bring about love which the Lawgiver has commanded.
